messages.subject: Categorical variables in hierarchical mixed-effects model
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I'm sorry to bother you all with a post that is really a simple question. But, I have gotten myself all confused with how to properly code a categorical variable in my models. Some context, I am running community N-mixture models, and I have three years worth of data, but rather than use a dynamic model I am including year as a covariate for both abundance and detection. For some reason I can't quite figure out how to properly index the three level "year" factor within the model structure. I've tried a couple different ways of doing this based on some different ways I'd been seeing it done, but where I'm at now (which nimble won't the abundance model is as follows

# Ecological model for true abundance (process model)
   for(k in 1:nspec){
      for (i in 1:nsite){
         a[i,k] ~ dbern(phi[k])   # zero-inflation
         N[i,k] ~ dpois(a[i,k] * lambda[i,k])
         log(lambda[i,k]) <- beta0[k] + beta1[k] * (1-year[i]) + beta2[k] * year[i] + beta3[k] * s2h[i] + beta4[k] * g2b[i] + beta5[k] * s2hQ[i] + beta6[k] * g2bQ[i] 
         # Compute presence/absence matrix z (for N > 0) from latent abundance
         z[i,k] <- step(N[i,k]-1)  # returns TRUE if N >= 0
      }
   }

Enter code here...

Where beta0 would be the intercept (year 1) and beta1 and beta2 the effects of years 2 and 3 respectively. The detection model looks similar. 

Any help would be much appreciated! 

Ben

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables in hierarchical mixed-effects model
parts:
Here are two common ways to do it.

Nested indexing:
log(lambda[i, k]) <- beta0[k, year[i] ] + <other effects>

where beta0 has three columns, and year is a vector of 1s, 2s, and 3s indicating which year  site i is from.  (You might have data from each site in each year, but in that case nsite must really be number of sites x number of years?)

0/1 Indicators for years 2 and 3:
log(lambda[i, k]) <- beta0[k] + beta1[k] * year2indicator[i] + beta2[k] * year3indicator[i]

where year2indicator[i] is 1 for year 2 data and 0 otherwise, and year3indicator is 1 for year 3 and 0 otherwise.  Then year 1 has intercept beta0, year 2 has intercept beta0+beta1, and year3 has intercept beta0 + beta2.

HTH
Perry

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Categorical variables in hierarchical mixed-effects model
parts:
I don't see the call to nimbleMCMC() that you're using, but my strong suspicion is that you're requesting summary=TRUE, for the posterior summary statistics, and further that the sampling of one or more model dimensions is not getting started correctly - my guess is due to bad initial values, or NA's somewhere in your model.  Anyway, I think the posterior samples contain NA's (probably), and then for determining the 95% BCI for the posterior summary statistics, R's quantile() function is complaining about the NA's.

I'd suggest you get the *samples* returned, which is the default (unless you use samples=FALSE), then look at the posterior samples, find which variable(s) have NA's (most likely), then that will point you toward what part(s) of the model are not sampling properly.

Make sense?

log(lambda[i, k]) <- beta0[k] + beta1[k] * year2indicator[i] + beta2[k] * year3indicator[i]

where year2indicator[i] is 1 for year 2 data and 0 otherwise, and year3indicator is 1 for year 3 and 0 otherwise.  Then year 1 has intercept beta0, year 2 has intercept beta0+beta1, and year3 has intercept beta0 + beta2.

HTH
Perry

On Thursday, February 20, 2020 at 12:03:21 PM UTC-5, Daniel Turek wrote:

I don't see the call to nimbleMCMC() that you're using, but my strong suspicion is that you're requesting summary=TRUE, for the posterior summary statistics, and further that the sampling of one or more model dimensions is not getting started correctly - my guess is due to bad initial values, or NA's somewhere in your model.  Anyway, I think the posterior samples contain NA's (probably), and then for determining the 95% BCI for the posterior summary statistics, R's quantile() function is complaining about the NA's.

I'd suggest you get the *samples* returned, which is the default (unless you use samples=FALSE), then look at the posterior samples, find which variable(s) have NA's (most likely), then that will point you toward what part(s) of the model are not sampling properly.

Make sense?
